definitions.explanation: An egg fried in a pan without flipping, so the yolk remains visible on top. The name literally means 'eyeball fry' because the round yolk resembles an eye.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}ごはんに{目玉焼|めだまや}きを{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a fried egg for breakfast.

examples.japanese: {目玉焼|めだまや}きには{醤油|しょうゆ}をかける{派|は}ですか。
examples.english: Are you the type to put soy sauce on your fried egg?

examples.japanese: {半熟|はんじゅく}の{目玉焼|めだまや}きを{乗|の}せたハンバーグが{人気|にんき}メニューだ。
examples.english: A hamburger steak topped with a soft-fried egg is a popular menu item.

notes:
A staple of Japanese home cooking and cafe menus. The name comes from {目玉|めだま} (eyeball) + {焼|や}き (fried), describing the appearance of the round yolk.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目玉焼|めだまや}きを{焼|や}く (to fry an egg)
- {半熟|はんじゅく}の{目玉焼|めだまや}き (soft-fried egg with runny yolk)
- {目玉焼|めだまや}き{丼|どん} (fried egg rice bowl)

CULTURAL NOTE:
What to put on a {目玉焼|めだまや}き is a common topic of friendly debate in Japan. Some prefer {醤油|しょうゆ} (soy sauce), others {塩|しお} (salt), ソース (Worcestershire sauce), or ケチャップ (ketchup).
